lessons.title: இ (i) — the letter that opens இல்லை
lessons.gloss: the single character இ — the letter that opens இல்லை

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: இ and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: read உ and ஓ aloud, and write each once.
Now say இல்லை (illai), "no". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.
இ — i.

It is the letter at the front of இல்லை (illai), "no", one of the first words in this book. You have been writing its sign, ◌ி, since நன்றி. This is the independent shape of the same vowel: the one a word uses when it begins with the sound.
1. start here: curl around the inner loop.
2. without lifting, sweep down the inner right curve.
3. without lifting, carry left and turn through the lower loop.
4. without lifting, climb the lower diagonal.
5. without lifting, carry right and turn around the lower loop, then lift.
6. put the pen down again and climb the outer left side.
7. without lifting, arch over the top and down the right — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 1.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order, not a national standard — Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation. Source: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 4, இ (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 192.

segments.instruction: இ three times, saying i as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: இ three times, saying *i* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: ஓ, then இ, from memory]

segments.text: Which character is this — இ? (i.) Which word did it come from? (இல்லை, illai, "no".)

lessons.title: ◌ை (ai) — the sign that ends இல்லை
lessons.gloss: the single character ◌ை — the sign that ends இல்லை

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on, your eyes, for letter shapes on the page and your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ◌ை and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: read ஓ and இ aloud, and write each once.
Now say இல்லை (illai), "no". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.

It is a vowel sign, not a letter. It attaches to a consonant and replaces the built-in a with ai. Look at the end of இல்லை: the sign sits on the left of ல, although you say it after. Tamil writes this sign first and sounds it second.
Put your pen on ◌ை (ai) and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

This book does not yet tell you where to start the character or which way to travel. That is a real thing, taught with real variation from school to school, and it is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.

lessons.title: ஸ (sa) — the letter inside நமஸ்காரம்
lessons.gloss: the single character ஸ — the letter inside நமஸ்காரம்

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ஸ and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: read இ and ◌ை (ai) aloud, and write each once.
Now say நமஸ்காரம் (namaskāram), "the borrowed bow-word". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.
ஸ — sa.

It is inside நமஸ்காரம் (namaskāram), the borrowed bow-word you met beside வணக்கம். ஸ (sa) is a Grantha letter: Tamil added it to write words that came from Sanskrit, so you will see it mostly in borrowed words.
Put your pen on ஸ (sa) and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

This book does not yet tell you where to start the character or which way to travel. That is a real thing, taught with real variation from school to school, and it is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
